title: Quasi-finite morphisms
statement:
Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a separated, quasi-finite morphism of finite
type of $k_0$-schemes, with $Y_0$ quasi-separated of finite type over
$k_0$. Then $R^if_{0!}F=0$ for every Weil sheaf $F$ and every $i>0$;
and if $F$ is $\iota$-mixed of weights at most $w$ (resp. has all local
Frobenius eigenvalues of weight at most $w$), then so is (resp. has)
$f_{0!}F=R^0f_{0!}F$.

proof.text: The target $Y_0$ is quasi-compact because it is of finite type over a field, and is quasi-separated by hypothesis. Apply [thm-pqf-zmt-factorization] to obtain $X_0\xrightarrow{j_0}T_0\xrightarrow{p_0}Y_0$, with $j_0$ quasi-compact open, $p_0$ finite, and $f_0=p_0j_0$. This is a compactification since a finite morphism is proper [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper]. It is over $k_0$, giving compatible geometric base changes. No absolute separatedness of $Y_0$ or $T_0$ is inferred. The false inference in the blueprint proof of lem-zl-quasi-finite is avoided: the identity of the affine line with doubled origin is a finite morphism whose source is not separated over $k_0$. The compact-support operation of [def-weil-integral-rational-qbar-compact-support] depends on a chosen compactification; by the comparison stated in [def-zl-weil-compact-support-cohomology] (for two compactifications of $f_0$, with no separatedness of $X_0,Y_0$ assumed, the higher images $R^n_cf_!F$ are isomorphic as Weil sheaves), every assertion of the item for an arbitrary compactification follows from the same assertion for $c_0=(j_0,p_0)$: vanishing, punctual bounds and mixedness are invariant under isomorphism of Weil sheaves. The remaining steps compute with $c_0$.

source.place: first paragraph, finite compactification; correction of the false absolute-separatedness inference

proof.text: For the finite compactification, apply [lem-zl-finite-compactification-weil-exact]. Transport positive-degree vanishing to the supplied compactification using [def-zl-weil-compact-support-cohomology]. Retain the exact degree-zero functor T and its object isomorphisms.

For each eigenvalue of T(F), apply [lem-zl-finite-compactification-eigenvalues]. If β^e is an eigenvalue at x, #κ(x)=#κ(y)^e and e is nonzero. Multiplicativity of the arbitrary embedding and of the norm gives the upper-bound inequality (or purity equality) after taking nonnegative e-th roots. Eigenvalue predicates are invariant under Weil isomorphisms by composing their finite-stage presentations.

Transport the input finite filtration term by term under T. Finite-limit preservation preserves the monomorphisms, and finite-colimit preservation identifies cokernels with T of the original quotients. The preceding purity calculation makes these quotients pure of their original weights. Map the zero initial term and final isomorphism, then compose with the isomorphism from T(F) to the prescribed higher image. This constructs exactly its mixed filtration, including length zero.

lean.statement: theorem sfQuasiFiniteCompactSupport (D : FiniteFieldDatum.{u}) (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (hl : l ≠ D.p) (Ω : Type v) [Field Ω] [Algebra (Padic l) Ω] [IsAlgClosure (Padic l) Ω] {X₀ Y₀ : Over (Spec (.of D.k₀))} [LocallyOfFiniteType X₀.hom] [QuasiCompact X₀.hom] [LocallyOfFiniteType Y₀.hom] [QuasiCompact Y₀.hom] [QuasiSeparated Y₀.hom] (f₀ : X₀ ⟶ Y₀) [IsSeparated f₀.left] (_hqf : Scheme.Hom.IsQuasiFinite f₀.left) (c : Compactification f₀.left) (F : sfCommonStageWeilSheaf D l hl X₀ Ω) : (∀ i : ℕ, 0 < i → IsZero (zlWeilHigherShriek D l hl Ω f₀ c i F)) ∧ ∀ (iota : Ω →+* ℂ) (w : ℝ), (SfIsMixedOfWeightsAtMost D l hl Ω X₀ iota F w → SfIsMixedOfWeightsAtMost D l hl Ω Y₀ iota (zlWeilHigherShriek D l hl Ω f₀ c 0 F) w) ∧ ((∀ (x : {x : X₀.left // x ∈ closedPoints X₀.left}) (α : Ω), SfPunctualEigenvalue D l hl Ω X₀ F x α → ‖iota α‖ ≤ (Nat.card (X₀.left.residueField x.val) : ℝ) ^ (w / 2)) → ∀ (y : {y : Y₀.left // y ∈ closedPoints Y₀.left}) (β : Ω), SfPunctualEigenvalue D l hl Ω Y₀ (zlWeilHigherShriek D l hl Ω f₀ c 0 F) y β → ‖iota β‖ ≤ (Nat.card (Y₀.left.residueField y.val) : ℝ) ^ (w / 2))
